# Sink-rule fixtures

One input the INTdfm rule layer saw, plus the findings `rules.py` returned for it, for
`sm.hole_spacing`, `sm.tolerance_across_bends` and the three countersink rules.

| Field | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| `source` | the INTdfm commit, its rule-layer hash, and the recording this case starts from |
| `case.group` | which rule function to run: `spacing`, `tolerance` or `countersinks` |
| `case.flat` | `rules.is_flat(solid)` for that part |
| `case.test_only` | `false` for a committed schema-2 recording; `true` for an edited one |
| `case.report_checked` | `true` when the recording's `expected.report` keeps this rule's finding unmerged and the generator checked the two agree; `null` when the report merges the cause across rules, so the rule layer's own finding is the only comparable one |
| `input` | `CheckInput`'s parts (`declared`, `generic`, `shop`, `facts`, `critical`) and the two gate findings the rules read |
| `expected.findings` | exactly what the Python function returns, before the report merges it |

Real cases come from `tests/fixtures/dfm-replay/v1` in the INTdfm checkout. No recording has a
spacing pair that misses its number, a declared critical dimension or a countersink, so those
cases edit a recording's facts (a moved hole, a shop table, a countersink) and are marked
`TEST-ONLY`. Their expected findings are still the Python rule layer's own output for that input,
generated by running the rule functions directly. Do not edit a fixture by hand and do not write
an expectation the Python layer did not produce.

The messages in a fixture are INTdfm's; Rust compares status, `error_code`, `reason_code`,
measured value, chosen limit, layer and rule list, and not the text. Regenerate from the INTdfm
checkout with the generator used for this batch (`PYTHONPATH=src`, no OCP).
